triangle-area.name: Area of a triangle
triangle-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies base by height and halves it to get the area of a triangle
triangle-area.description: The area of a triangle is its base length times its height, divided by 2. Cutting a rectangle along a diagonal gives two triangles, which is why the area comes out as half the rectangle's.

b.description: The length of the bottom side of the triangle.

h.description: The perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex.

\\frac{1}{2}.description: It means half of the rectangle.

realWorldExamples: Finding the triangular area of a roof
Working out how much fabric a triangular flag takes

rectangle-area.name: Area of a rectangle
rectangle-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies length by width to get the area of a rectangle
rectangle-area.description: The area of a rectangle is its length times its width. In a quadrilateral whose four angles are all right angles, this is the same as counting how many unit squares fit in one row and multiplying by the number of rows.

l.description: The horizontal length of the rectangle.

w.description: The vertical length of the rectangle.

realWorldExamples: Finding the floor area of a room
Working out the area of a blackboard
Comparing smartphone screen sizes

square-area.name: Area of a square
square-area.oneLiner: The formula that squares the side length to get the area of a square
square-area.description: The area of a square is the length of one side multiplied by itself. Since all four sides are the same length, it works on the same principle as the area of a rectangle whose length and width are equal.

s.description: The length of one side of the square.

s^2.description: The side length multiplied by itself.

realWorldExamples: Finding the area of a single tile
Working out the size of a square picture frame

parallelogram-area.name: Area of a parallelogram
parallelogram-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies base by height to get the area of a parallelogram
parallelogram-area.description: The area of a parallelogram is its base length times its height. Cut a parallelogram and slide the piece over and you get a rectangle, which is why the formula has the same shape as the one for a rectangle.

b.description: The length of the bottom side of the parallelogram.

h.description: The perpendicular distance between the two parallel sides.

realWorldExamples: Working out the area of a slanted window pane
The size of a parallelogram-shaped desk cover

trapezoid-area.name: Area of a trapezoid
trapezoid-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies the sum of the two parallel sides by the height and halves it
trapezoid-area.description: The area of a trapezoid is the lengths of the two parallel sides (the top and the bottom) added together, multiplied by the height, and divided by 2. Flip a second copy of the trapezoid and join it on and you get a parallelogram; this is half of that, which is where the 2 comes from.

a.description: The length of the upper parallel side of the trapezoid.

b.description: The length of the lower parallel side of the trapezoid.

h.description: The perpendicular distance between the two parallel sides.

\\frac{1}{2}.description: It means half of the parallelogram.

realWorldExamples: Finding the area of a trapezoid-shaped flower bed
Working out the area of a trapezoid roof

rhombus-area.name: Area of a rhombus
rhombus-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies the two diagonals and halves the result to get the area of a rhombus
rhombus-area.description: The area of a rhombus is the product of its two diagonal lengths divided by 2. The two diagonals of a rhombus meet at right angles, and cutting along them and rearranging the pieces gives half of a rectangle.

d_1.description: The length of one diagonal of the rhombus.

d_2.description: The length of the other diagonal of the rhombus.

\\frac{1}{2}.description: It means half of the rectangle.

realWorldExamples: Working out the area of a rhombus-cut gem
Finding how much fabric a kite takes

circle-area-elem.name: Area of a circle
circle-area-elem.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies the square of the radius by pi to get the area of a circle
circle-area-elem.description: The area of a circle is the radius squared times pi. Slice a circle into very thin wedges and lay them out and you get something close to a rectangle whose length is half the circumference and whose width is the radius — and that gives this formula.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The distance from the center of the circle to its edge.

realWorldExamples: Comparing pizza sizes
Finding the area of a round clock face
Working out the area of a coin

circle-circumference.name: Circumference of a circle
circle-circumference.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies twice the radius by pi to get the circumference of a circle
circle-circumference.description: The circumference of a circle is twice the radius — that is, the diameter — times pi. The distance you travel going once around the circle is exactly its circumference.

C.description: The total length measured along the outer edge of the circle.

2.description: The factor that turns the radius into the diameter.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

r.description: The distance from the center of the circle to its edge.

realWorldExamples: The distance a bicycle wheel covers in one full turn
The length of one lap of a circular track

sector-area.name: Area of a sector
sector-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies the square of the radius by the central angle and halves it to get the area of a sector
sector-area.description: The area of a sector is the radius squared times the central angle in radians, divided by 2. A sector is a slice of a circle, so the bigger the central angle, the bigger the area.

\\theta.description: The angle opened out from the center of the sector (in radians).

\\frac{1}{2}.description: The coefficient in the area formula.

realWorldExamples: The area a clock's minute hand sweeps out
The area of a single slice of pizza

arc-length.name: Arc length
arc-length.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies the radius by the central angle to get the length of an arc
arc-length.description: The length of an arc is the radius times the central angle in radians. An arc is a piece of the circumference, and when the central angle is a full turn (2 pi) the arc length equals the whole circumference.

l.description: The length of a portion of the circle's edge.

r.description: The distance from the center of the circle to its edge.

\\theta.description: The central angle the arc subtends (in radians).

realWorldExamples: The length of a curved stretch of roller coaster track
The arc length between the marks on a clock face

rectangle-perimeter.name: Perimeter of a rectangle
rectangle-perimeter.oneLiner: The formula that doubles the sum of the length and the width to get the perimeter of a rectangle
rectangle-perimeter.description: The perimeter of a rectangle is the length plus the width, multiplied by 2. Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so adding one length and one width and doubling gives the total of all four sides.

P.description: The total length of the rectangle's four sides.

l.description: The horizontal length of the rectangle.

w.description: The vertical length of the rectangle.

2.description: You multiply by 2 because there are two pairs of opposite sides.

realWorldExamples: Working out the length of the border of a picture frame
The distance run along the edge of a sports field

triangle-perimeter.name: Perimeter of a triangle
triangle-perimeter.oneLiner: The formula that adds all three side lengths to get the perimeter of a triangle
triangle-perimeter.description: The perimeter of a triangle is the sum of the lengths of its three sides. It is the same as the total distance you travel going once around the triangle's edge.

P.description: The total length of the triangle's three sides.

a.description: The length of the first side of the triangle.

b.description: The length of the second side of the triangle.

c.description: The length of the third side of the triangle.

realWorldExamples: The total length of a triangular fence
How much cord it takes to trim the edge of a triangular flag

regular-polygon-area.name: Area of a regular polygon
regular-polygon-area.oneLiner: The formula that gets the area of a regular polygon from the number of sides, the side length, and the apothem
regular-polygon-area.description: The area of a regular polygon is the number of sides times the side length times the apothem (the perpendicular distance from the center to a side), divided by 2. Split the polygon into triangles from the center and this is the same as adding up the areas of all those triangles.

A.description: The area the regular polygon covers.

n.description: How many sides the regular polygon has.

s.description: The length of one side of the regular polygon.

a.description: The perpendicular distance from the center to the midpoint of a side.

\\frac{1}{2}.description: The coefficient that comes from the triangle area formula.

realWorldExamples: The area of one hexagonal cell in a honeycomb
The area of a pentagonal star ornament

annulus-area.name: Area of an annulus
annulus-area.oneLiner: The formula that multiplies the difference of the squared radii by pi to get the area of a ring
annulus-area.description: The area of an annulus (a ring shape) is the area of the outer circle minus the area of the inner one. Subtract the square of the small radius from the square of the large one and multiply by pi.

A.description: The area the annulus (ring shape) covers.

\\pi.description: The circumference of a circle divided by its diameter, about 3.14159.

R.description: The radius of the larger outer circle.

r.description: The radius of the smaller inner circle.

R^2 - r^2.description: The square of the inner radius subtracted from the square of the outer radius.

realWorldExamples: Finding the area of the top of a doughnut
The area of a circular running lane

triangle-angle-sum.name: Angle sum of a triangle
triangle-angle-sum.oneLiner: The property that the three interior angles of a triangle always add up to 180 degrees
triangle-angle-sum.description: The angle sum property says that adding the angles at all three vertices of a triangle always gives 180 degrees, a half turn. This holds for any triangle at all — acute, right, or obtuse — the three interior angles always add to 180 degrees.

\\alpha.description: The angle at the first vertex of the triangle.

\\beta.description: The angle at the second vertex of the triangle.

\\gamma.description: The angle at the third vertex of the triangle.

180°.description: The angle a straight line makes, which equals the angle sum of a triangle.

realWorldExamples: Finding the remaining angle when you know two of them
Getting the angles right on a triangular structure in construction
